Prostate-specific antigen monitoring
Measurement of PSA is the cornerstone of follow-up after local treatment. While PSA thresholds depend on the
local treatment used, PSA recurrence almost always precedes clinical recurrence [1436, 1437]. The key question
is to establish when a PSA rise is clinically significant since not all PSA increases have the same clinical value
(see Section 6.4.2) [994]. No prospective studies are available on the optimal timing for PSA testing and the
impact on oncological outcomes.

interventions.body:
REGISTRAR
WHAT I FOUND
**radiology_report**: The mpMRI prostate showed a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone with seminal vesicle involvement. The prostate volume was 57.28 mL, and the PSA density was 3.26 ng/mL/mL. The impression noted clinical stage cT1c.
**pathology_report**: The biopsy specimen from February 2023 revealed adenocarcinoma of the prostate with a Gleason score of 4+4 (ISUP grade group 4). The tumour exhibited a predominant cribriform growth pattern and perineural invasion, located in the seminal vesicles on the right.
**previous_notes**: The prior note from February 2023 documented a PI-RADS 5 lesion, a Gleason 4+4 diagnosis with perineural invasion, and the patient opting for active surveillance.
**family_history**: No family history was recorded.
**psa_trend**: The PSA trend shows a significant escalation: 17.4 ng/mL in Feb 2023, 10.2 ng/mL in Jun 2024, 0.5 ng/mL in Oct 2024, and 187.0 ng/mL in Feb 2025.
**laboratory_results**: The most recent PSA was 187.0 ng/mL (as of Jan 2025), with a %Free PSA of 15%. Other labs (Hb, WBC, Platelets, Creatinine, eGFR, Testosterone, ALP, LDH) were within normal or acceptable ranges.

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED
The specific findings from the moderator's requested documents regarding the overall management decision are not recorded.

WHAT THIS SUPPORTS
The retrieved data strongly supports the need for aggressive management. The PI-RADS 5 MRI with seminal vesicle involvement, combined with the high PSA level (187.0 ng/mL) and the history of high-grade disease (Gleason 4+4 with PIN) from the prior biopsy, aligns with the expert opinion leaning towards active treatment. The PSA trend confirms rapid progression. The pathology confirms the aggressive nature of the disease.

previous_notes.author: Dr. H. Martens (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with elevated PSA of 17.4 ng/mL in February 2023. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. Multiparametric MRI was arranged, showing a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone. Transperineal biopsy was performed, revealing Gleason 4+4 (ISUP grade group 4) adenocarcinoma with cribriform pattern and perineural invasion. The patient was referred to urology for further management discussion. At that time, he opted for active surveillance after reviewing the risks and benefits of immediate intervention, citing his age and comorbidities. Follow-up PSA was scheduled for six months later.
